journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Professional Development: Attendees' Perceptions from Previous PD Opportunities/Preferences for Follow-up Activities
text_snippet: Professional Development: Attendees' Perceptions from Previous PD Opportunities/Preferences for Follow-up Activities The purpose of this study was to examine the perceptions attendees have of Professional Development meetings. In addition, attendees were asked to state their preferences for PD follow-up. Data were analyzed in terms of attendee assignment, and career stage (based on Huberman, 1989). Results indicated that both assignment and career stage were not significantly related to perception. Follow-up preferences were varied, indicating individual needs. This information is important for PD providers, who must be kept accountable to attendees for relevant information.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Large Language Models in Mathematics Education: Practitioners as Pedagogical Prompt Engineers
text_snippet: Large Language Models in Mathematics Education: Practitioners as Pedagogical Prompt Engineers Effective classroom integration of large language models (LLMs) requires domain-specific Prompt Engineering (PE) competence among teachers and students. Existing PE literature remains largely technical or cross-disciplinary, offering limited guidance for mathematics education, where LLMs continue to struggle with mathematical reasoning. This paper proposes a pedagogically grounded framework that positions educators as pedagogical prompt engineers who scaffold students’ interactions with LLMs through discipline-specific prompting practices. The framework provides structured classroom exemplars to enhance mathematical reasoning, conceptual understanding, and critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs. By fostering critical AI literacy and human-centered inquiry, it supports deeper, reflective, and ethical engagement with intelligent technologies.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Developing Professional Readiness in Business Students: An Integrative Framework Linking Cognitive Load Management and Capability Formation
text_snippet: Developing Professional Readiness in Business Students: An Integrative Framework Linking Cognitive Load Management and Capability Formation Professional readiness in business education is often treated as an outcome of course completion, grades, content exposure, or career preparation, yet these markers do not adequately account for how students develop the capacity to translate learning into responsible professional action. This theory-informed conceptual article integrates cognitive load theory, business education scholarship, employability and work-readiness research, and the capabilities approach. It develops the Business Student Professional Readiness Framework, which traces a developmental pathway from learning complexity through cognitive load management, knowledge integration, and capability formation to professional readiness. Four propositions articulate these relationships and, together, establish the framework’s developmental logic.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Zoom Me In, Zoom Me Out, Zoom Me All About: Graduate Students' Perceptions of Zoom Meetings in Online Graduate Programs
text_snippet: Zoom Me In, Zoom Me Out, Zoom Me All About: Graduate Students' Perceptions of Zoom Meetings in Online Graduate Programs This quantitative study examined the perceptions of online graduate students regarding Zoom meetings conducted within their courses. The population included all students enrolled in online graduate educational leadership courses at a four-year university. Using convenience sampling, the final sample consisted of 217 graduate students who completed all survey items (N = 227 consenting participants total). An anonymous online survey of 12 items was distributed via Qualtrics. The first four questions collected demographic information; the remaining eight addressed perceived engagement, reasons for limited engagement, and overall perceptions of Zoom meetings. Descriptive statistics, multiple regression analysis, and analysis of variance (ANOVA) were used to analyze data in response to three research questions. Results indicated that liking the Zoom format and attendance frequency were the strongest predictors of perceived Zoom meeting value. Gender and education level did not significantly predict Zoom perceptions.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Re-thinking the Role of Corporate Reporting: Supporting Students in the Transition
text_snippet: Re-thinking the Role of Corporate Reporting: Supporting Students in the Transition We are living in a changing business world, in which sustainability strategies are increasingly integrated into core business operations. As business models evolve to reflect these changes, so must corporate reporting, requiring future employees to develop novel competencies. Considering that defining and reporting material environmental and social topics is critical to credible sustainability reporting, we developed a learning module (used either online or as a class presentation) that addresses key materiality concepts. Furthermore, our analysis adds to the literature relating to the effectiveness of online or in-person sustainability education modules. Student reviewers completed pre- and post-surveys assessing their own knowledge and opinions about material environmental and social topics and their connection to financial reporting. The analysis of the responses showed a significant increase in learning and a change in some opinions about corporate reporting after the student reviewers completed the materiality segments. We found that such resources (online or in-person) can support students’ learning about the changing corporate reporting context, which could lead to more in-d

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Nigerian Teachers’ Framing of Physics within a Colonial Context
text_snippet: Nigerian Teachers’ Framing of Physics within a Colonial Context Physics education in Nigeria is often criticized for being overly theoretical and disconnected from students’ cultural contexts and everyday lives. This study examines how two in-service physics teachers navigate systemic and colonial constraints while making physics more relevant to their students. Drawing on framing theory, culturally relevant pedagogy (CRP), and coloniality, the study uses interviews to explore teachers’ approaches to classroom practice. Findings reveal that curricula and professional development continue to privilege Western epistemologies and canonical physics knowledge. However, teachers demonstrate agency and resourcefulness by incorporating students’ local knowledge, including farming practices, musical traditions, and community challenges, to connect textbook concepts with real-world applications. This culturally relevant work remains largely informal and teacher-driven, operating within a system shaped by colonial assumptions about valid scientific knowledge. The study argues for reimagining physics education in Nigeria by moving beyond deficit views of teachers and recognizing their agency in reframing physics instruction. journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Determinants of Effective Experiential Learning Experiences in ISYE Senior Design Capstone Courses: An Eight-Year Analysis
text_snippet: Determinants of Effective Experiential Learning Experiences in ISYE Senior Design Capstone Courses: An Eight-Year Analysis Recent studies have explored the benefits of senior design capstone courses; however, there remains a lack of empirical research categorizing project taxonomies and quantifying the specific pedagogical benefits unique to Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISYE) capstone experiences. This study aims to: 1) categorize the different types of projects in which students choose to engage, 2) map course subjects and skillsets utilized in these senior design capstone projects, 3) contrast best practices for teaching a senior design capstone project, and 4) provide insights on achievements gained through the senior design capstone course. This study presents a longitudinal analysis of Senior Design Capstone projects spanning an eight-year period. By examining ISYE-specific data using statistical analysis, the research identifies evolving patterns in project selection and the consistent skillsets required for professional success. Our results show that teams who select industry projects, start planning early, leverage team members’ strengths, and work cohesively with clear roles tend to perform better in oral presentations, reports, and video deliverables, often leading to recognition or aw

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Using AI for Rubric Based Grading: A Practical Guide for Instructors
text_snippet: Using AI for Rubric Based Grading: A Practical Guide for Instructors This paper describes using artificial intelligence as part of rubric-based grading for student writing assignments. Particularly, AI can help instructors with parts of the grading process, such as checking whether a submission meets assignment requirements, comparing a paper to the rubric categories, suggesting draft scores, and outlining possible feedback for instructor review. While providing an example of instructions given to AI programs, this paper also identifies several problems with AI based rubric grading. AI can be useful in rubric-based grading, but only when it is kept in a limited role and used in support of the instructor’s judgment.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: The Lack of Formal Power in Academia: Common Scenarios for Department Chairs That Make Serving Problematic
text_snippet: The Lack of Formal Power in Academia: Common Scenarios for Department Chairs That Make Serving Problematic Managing within academia can be highly problematic due to a myriad of factors. The current work seeks to identify common scenarios that compound the ability of effective management within academia. The focus of the discussion will center on arguably the most difficult managerial role within academia, the department chair. Specifically, the current work identifies scenarios detrimental to effective management for the department chair, discusses why these scenarios are problematic, and then provides practical approaches for how institutions of higher education may address these situations in a way that best serves the needs of the institution.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: An Assessment of the Effectiveness of the Internal Audit at the University of Sierra Leone
text_snippet: An Assessment of the Effectiveness of the Internal Audit at the University of Sierra Leone Internal auditing is essential for evaluating and improving internal controls, risk management, and governance in government entities. By identifying weaknesses and recommending improvements, it enhances accountability, resource utilization, and public trust. Internal audits complement the work of Supreme Audit Institutions (SAIs), which provide independent external assessments of financial management, legal compliance, and stewardship of public resources. Together, they promote transparency, accountability, and effective public financial management. A robust control system supported by risk-based approaches and stakeholder engagement further strengthens governance and efficient resource use. This study employed a concurrent triangulation mixed-methods approach to assess the internal audit function at the University of Sierra Leone. Findings reveal that the internal audit department is inadequately resourced to perform its responsibilities effectively. Although segregation of duties and access to information are maintained, the department requires a functional audit committee, additional qualified auditors, and auditing software to improve operational effectiveness. journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Student Brand Engagement and Engagement Marketing Behaviors in Higher Education
text_snippet: Student Brand Engagement and Engagement Marketing Behaviors in Higher Education Students are uniquely positioned to perform engagement marketing behaviors that benefit higher education institution (HEI) brands, yet research on student brand engagement remains limited. This study examines drivers of student brand engagement from marketing such as brand attachment, self-brand connection, brand loyalty, psychological engagement, and perceived career preparation. Survey data from students were analyzed using stepwise regression, moderation, and mediation models. Students actively support the HEI through word-of-mouth behaviors, social media activity, wearing branded clothing, and recommending the college. Findings reveal nuanced relationships, including negative effects of brand attachment, highlighting the critical role of brand loyalty in shaping engagement.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: A One-week Module for Introducing Agile to Business Students Using a Jira Learning Path
text_snippet: A One-week Module for Introducing Agile to Business Students Using a Jira Learning Path Given the widespread organizational adoption of agile methodologies, this paper addresses the growing need for business graduates to understand agile principles. Recognizing limited curriculum time, we design and implement a one-week module introducing agile concepts and the Kanban and Scrum frameworks. The module includes a 75-minute lecture and an assignment based on an online Jira learning path. Designed for students with little or no prior exposure to agile concepts, the module provides foundational knowledge for future applications or advanced study. We evaluate the effectiveness of the module through qualitative and quantitative analyses and discuss its implications for integrating agile content into business education.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Reimagining Career and Community Colleges in an Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Entry-Level Preparation to Lifelong Capability Ecosystems
text_snippet: Reimagining Career and Community Colleges in an Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Entry-Level Preparation to Lifelong Capability Ecosystems Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labor markets in ways that extend beyond changes in skill demand to the mechanisms through which individuals gain access to work. Career and community colleges have traditionally served as pathways to employment by preparing learners for early-career roles where formal learning is converted into applied capability. This paper argues that this model is under increasing pressure. Drawing on task-based theories of technological change and empirical evidence from 2022–2026, it shows how AI is compressing the routine cognitive tasks that historically defined many entry-level positions. As these tasks are automated or augmented, organizations are redesigning jobs to deliver immediate productivity, reducing opportunities for learning-by-doing and weakening traditional signals of competence and potential. The result is a growing problem of recognition failure: a mismatch between how capabilities are developed and how competence is validated and trusted. Using Canadian labor-market data and international case studies from Tecnológico de Monterrey and Brainport Eindhoven, the paper explores emerging institutional responses and outlines implications f

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: A Boon or Bane? Challenges and Opportunities of AI Adoption in Higher Education
text_snippet: A Boon or Bane? Challenges and Opportunities of AI Adoption in Higher Education Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping higher education by transforming how students learn, how faculty teach, and how institutions manage academic processes. While AI offers opportunities for autonomy, competence, collaboration, and efficiency, it also raises concerns of dependency, quasi-plagiarism, and academic dishonesty. This conceptual paper synthesizes insights from ten institutional cases across global contexts and draws on five theoretical foundations, Diffusion of Innovation, the Technology Acceptance Model, Self-Determination Theory, Social Learning Theory, and Academic Integrity frameworks, to propose a process model of AI adoption and use in higher education. The model explains how faculty engagement, institutional policy, student motivation, peer norms, and integrity enforcement interact to shape learning outcomes, distinguishing authentic use of AI from misuse. By addressing policy gaps, governance challenges, and equity concerns, the study contributes to theory by advancing multi-framework integration and to practice by offering strategies for ethical, responsible, and sustainable AI adoption in higher education.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Operationalizing ChatGPT in Coursework: Assignment Compliance, Prompt Use, and Implementation Challenges
text_snippet: Operationalizing ChatGPT in Coursework: Assignment Compliance, Prompt Use, and Implementation Challenges This study examines the implementation of a ChatGPT-supported assignment in an undergraduate organizational behavior course. Student teams were asked to submit draft blog content to ChatGPT, use the feedback to revise their work, and document the process as part of the assignment. Across two assignments, the analysis focused on prompt use, assignment criteria, follow-up prompting, submission compliance, and attempts required to meet expectations. Findings highlight the need for stronger scaffolds, clearer documentation structures, and greater support for AI literacy when integrating generative AI into coursework.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: From Coding to Lesson Planning: Developing TPACK Through Robotics in a Mathematics Methods Course
text_snippet: From Coding to Lesson Planning: Developing TPACK Through Robotics in a Mathematics Methods Course It is essential for PSTs to transition from their studies to classrooms with the tools and strategies to implement effective instructional practices. This mixed-methods research investigated how educational robotics instruction in two mathematics methods courses informed pre-service teachers’ (PSTs) TPACK. Conducted with middle grades and secondary PSTs using Dash and TI-Innovator Rover (robots), the quantitative findings revealed statistically significant results for PCK, TCK, TPK, and TPACK for the Spring 2024 cohort. However, the Fall 2023 results revealed statistically significant effects only in the TCK and TPK domains. The qualitative data analysis revealed that PSTs gained an understanding of how to teach with robotics to support conceptual understanding of mathematical topics, but robotics alone cannot support TPACK development. This research answered calls to provide training on educational technologies over a longer period, to develop context-based learning activities, and to compare knowledge with competency. When teacher preparation programs incorporate educational technology training into methods courses, they may simultaneously support future school district needs whi

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: The Impact of Covid-19 Distruption on Online Learning Across Disciplines in Post-Secondary Business Education
text_snippet: The Impact of Covid-19 Distruption on Online Learning Across Disciplines in Post-Secondary Business Education A large body of research has focused on the impact of internal and external variables on instructional quality and key metrics related to classroom performance, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic. Recently, findings have indicated significant impact on student performance in both face-to-face and online course modalities. This work addresses a gap in the most recent work by assessing how the discipline or subject matter being taught influences these outcomes in online course delivery. Results show that the discipline a course is housed in has a significant impact on key student performance metrics. Results and future research are discussed.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Comparing Student Challenges During COVID-19 Across Higher Education Institutions in Four Countries: A Mixed Methods Analysis Using the Shannon Diversity Index
text_snippet: Comparing Student Challenges During COVID-19 Across Higher Education Institutions in Four Countries: A Mixed Methods Analysis Using the Shannon Diversity Index This mixed methods research study compares the diversity of challenges experienced by university students during COVID-19 across five institutional contexts in four countries: South Africa (two universities), the United States, Brazil, and Chile. Using previously published thematic findings, themes were quantitized and analyzed via the Shannon Diversity Index (SDI), yielding what is termed the Shannon-Based Thematic Diversity Index (SBTDI), which captures both the range and evenness of challenges. Results indicate variability in thematic diversity across institutions, with the New York sample showing the highest diversity and Wits University the lowest. Findings suggest that student challenges are multidimensional, underscoring the importance of designing comprehensive interventions for future pandemics and other large-scale disruptions.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: The Future of Higher Education in the Context of a Shrinking Student Population in Europe: A Prospective Demographic Analysis of University Systems in Spain and Italy
text_snippet: The Future of Higher Education in the Context of a Shrinking Student Population in Europe: A Prospective Demographic Analysis of University Systems in Spain and Italy Over the last few decades, Spain and Italy have undergone profound shifts in their demographic structures as other European countries, resulting in significant fluctuations in enrollment rates across Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and a remarkable expansion of private education providers. Focusing on both national contexts and their respective central Higher Educations hubs -Madrid Region (Comunidad de Madrid) in Spain and Lazio Region (Regione Lazio) in Italy- this paper analyzes demographic trends and the evolution of student enrollment in public and private universities. Furthermore, the study provides a projection of the potential student population through 2040, revealing an imminent long-term contraction of the student body. The findings highlight key implications, including a potential threat to the financial sustainability of public institutions and an intensification of institutional competition against a backdrop of population decline. Finally, based on the comparative regional analysis, this paper offers public policy recommendations and structural reforms aimed at mitigating the impact of this future sociodemographic reality in the two countries studied, ensuring

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: The Impact of Data Analytics and Statistics Instruction (DASI) On Student Learning: An Exploratory Study
text_snippet: The Impact of Data Analytics and Statistics Instruction (DASI) On Student Learning: An Exploratory Study In an increasingly data-driven world, Data Analytics and Statistics Instruction (DASI) has emerged as a transformative pedagogical approach that fundamentally reshapes how students engage with quantitative reasoning and evidence-based decision-making. This research paper examines the multidimensional impact of DASI on student learning outcomes, exploring how integrating real-world datasets, interactive analytical tools, and interdisciplinary applications enhances cognitive development, critical thinking, and practical skill acquisition. Through synthesis of empirical research, case studies, and theoretical frameworks, this paper demonstrates that DASI not only improves students' technical competencies but also cultivates essential 21st-century skills, including data literacy, analytical reasoning, and evidence-based communication. The findings reveal that effective DASI implementation requires careful attention to pedagogical design, technological infrastructure, instructor preparation, and assessment strategies that align with contemporary workforce demands and academic standards.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Reconnecting Critical Theory with Its Suffering Origins: Adorno, Auschwitz, and Maslow in Pedagogical Practice
text_snippet: Reconnecting Critical Theory with Its Suffering Origins: Adorno, Auschwitz, and Maslow in Pedagogical Practice With the growth of performed suffering in public discourse, contemporary critical theory faces challenges in both its practical application and public scrutiny. This study calls for alteration in the pedagogy of critical theory that re-centers the field with needed examination of the historical foundations that drove its origins, namely economic despair and dangerous oppression, with an effort to improve the instruction practices of critical theory with principles that focus on prudent student application. A richer integration of historically grounded examinations of suffering equips students with a reflexive lens for addressing challenges across different ages.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Being/Becoming Invisible: Trans and/or Nonbinary Gender Expression and Academic Experiences
text_snippet: Being/Becoming Invisible: Trans and/or Nonbinary Gender Expression and Academic Experiences Drawing on findings from a recent study, this paper examines how genderism and cisnormativity shape identity development and academic experiences of Trans and/or Nonbinary undergraduates. Centering participants’ narratives on gender expressions and perceptions by others, the study revealed persistent invisibility of gender identity based on genderist and cisnormative expectations. Academic experiences and development diverged between students who passed and wanted to be perceived as Cisgender and those who could not or chose not to do so. The paper concludes with recommendations for educators and institutions to better support Trans and/or Nonbinary students’ academic success.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Implementation of SCALE-UP in First-Year Chemistry at an HBCU
text_snippet: Implementation of SCALE-UP in First-Year Chemistry at an HBCU This study examines the implementation of the Student-Centered Active Learning Environment with Upside-down Pedagogies (SCALE-UP) in the first-year Chemistry course sequence for STEM majors at Hampton University, an HBCU. STEM majors at Hampton University must earn a grade of C or higher in all courses; grades below this threshold are designated STEM-FAIL. In Fall 2021, Chemistry 201 students were divided into a control lecture section and two SCALE-UP sections, all of which had identical assessments. Results showed lower STEM-FAIL rates (24% and 25%) in SCALE-UP sections compared to the lecture section (28%). In Spring 2022, both Chemistry 202 sections used SCALE-UP, and despite their differing enrollment sizes, they had identical STEM-FAIL rates (29%). This study revealed that SCALE-UP can be implemented at Hampton University. Additionally, the supportive environment and class sizes of under 60 students may also enhance student success.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Apprenticeship after AI: Bridging Gaps in Early-Career Knowledge-Work Roles
text_snippet: Apprenticeship after AI: Bridging Gaps in Early-Career Knowledge-Work Roles Artificial intelligence and automation are restructuring early-career knowledge-work roles by compressing the entry-level functions through which graduates historically built portfolios, developed professional judgment, and earned professional credibility. This paper argues that higher education has misdiagnosed the resulting challenge as curriculum misalignment—a content problem assumed to be solvable through revised syllabi, AI electives, and marginal expansions of experiential learning. Evidence from a systematic review of eighteen peer-reviewed studies and current labor-market analyses suggests a different conclusion: the informal post-degree apprenticeship system that historically completed graduate formation no longer reliably exists, and the architecture of the undergraduate degree is structurally incapable of replacing it through curricular revision alone. In response, this paper proposes the Embedded Formation Degree (EFD), a four-component framework consisting of accelerated domain entry, a four-year AI fluency track, an embedded practice firm, and structurally integrated employer partners. The framework reframes the education–employer gap as a structural failure in the p

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Project-Based Learning and Undergraduate Research in Environmental Education: Insights from a Case Study of Food Insecurity and SNAP/EBT Policy in Hawaiʻi
text_snippet: Project-Based Learning and Undergraduate Research in Environmental Education: Insights from a Case Study of Food Insecurity and SNAP/EBT Policy in Hawaiʻi Integration of project-based learning with undergraduate research provides a practical link between classroom learning, real environmental and social challenges. This paper examines how integrating undergraduate research with project-based learning can strengthen research practice, community engagement, and policy-relevant work in environmental and social science education. Using a case study of student-led research on food security policies in Hawaiʻi, with particular attention to SNAP (Supplementary Nutrition Assistance Program)/Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) programs, the paper examines how applied research experiences contribute to student learning and community engagement. Institutional initiatives such as the Undergraduate Research Opportunities Program (UROP) and the CTAHR Summer Research Institute provide the structure and support necessary for these experiences. The paper also discusses implications for curriculum design, institutional support, and the role of undergraduate research in environmental education.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Intellectual Effort Inflection Point and Generative Artificial Intelligence-driven Epistemic Delegation
text_snippet: Intellectual Effort Inflection Point and Generative Artificial Intelligence-driven Epistemic Delegation Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) enables students to produce polished assignments without demonstrating the intellectual effort that higher education is meant to cultivate. This paper reframes GenAI not as a detection problem but as an instructional design challenge. Drawing on experiential learning theory and behavioral objective design, we develop the Delegation Spectrum Model and the Intellectual Effort Inflection Point (IEIP) to describe how epistemic labor is distributed between students and GenAI across stages of mediation. Using Refined Disclosure of Support Statements from a senior communication course and AI prompt stress testing of a high-stakes memo assignment, we illustrate how task architecture can permit cognitive displacement while preserving surface quality. We then propose design principles for epistemically visible objectives that require source engagement, evidence appraisal, and claim warranting. The framework offers a transferable diagnostic tool for AI-resilient curriculum reform and for clarifying when epistemic delegation supports learning and when it undermines it.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Enduring Impact of Covid-19 on Accounting Majors at Hispanic Serving Institutions
text_snippet: Enduring Impact of Covid-19 on Accounting Majors at Hispanic Serving Institutions The COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted the CPA profession and Hispanic representation within it, yet post-pandemic evidence remains limited. After the pandemic, accounting degrees declined at HSIs and non-HSIs, and fewer graduates attempted the CPA Exam. While HSI graduates’ pass share improved, total sections decreased. The percentage of HSI candidates earning the CPA fell more than at non-HSIs, raising renewed concerns about Hispanic representation in the pipeline and prompting discussion of institutional and professional responses.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: ADHD and Student Grades: A Study of Student Grades and the Effectiveness of Common Treatments for Students with ADHD
text_snippet: ADHD and Student Grades: A Study of Student Grades and the Effectiveness of Common Treatments for Students with ADHD Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is among the most common neurodevelopmental conditions affecting school-age children, yet questions remain about which interventions most effectively support academic performance across different student populations. Using data from the U.S. Census Bureau's National Survey of Children's Health (n = 27,635), this study employs logistic regression to examine two questions: how does ADHD affect student grades, and which commonly used treatments are most effective at improving academic outcomes? ADHD was associated with a 12.2 percentage point increase in the likelihood of receiving low grades. Among treatments, medication and exercise were the only interventions that significantly reduced this likelihood, with effects varying meaningfully by gender and educational level. Notably, medication benefited male students but showed no significant effect for females, while exercise produced stronger academic benefits for females than males. No treatment showed a statistically significant effect for elementary school students. journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Revisiting Care in Higher Education: A Post-COVID Discussion
text_snippet: Revisiting Care in Higher Education: A Post-COVID Discussion While care in higher education is not commonly discussed, the COVID-19 pandemic has placed a spotlight on why tertiary institutions must reevaluate their policies, practices, and support systems to better meet students' needs. Research conducted during and after the COVID-19 pandemic has revealed a rise in mental health issues, feelings of isolation, insecurities related to employment, housing, and food, as well as grief associated with losses amongst college and university students. Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, its impacts on college and university students continue to shape higher education. This discussion explores why caring in higher education matters more than ever and why post-secondary institutions must be intentional about embedding structures of care to support student learning and well-being.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Factors Influencing Women’s Access to Education in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo: An Empirical Analysis
text_snippet: Factors Influencing Women’s Access to Education in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo: An Empirical Analysis This study analyzes the factors affecting women’s access to education in North Kivu Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, where prevailing customs and practices often limit their educational opportunities. Using a qualitative approach based on interviews, discriminant analysis and multinomial logistic regression were conducted to identify the variables that discriminate against and/or explain women’s access to education. The results indicate that parents’ level of education, the type of union between parents, parental income, and the religious affiliation of the head of household significantly influence the level of education attained by women.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Level of Satisfaction of Undergraduate Students With the Academic and Administrative Services Provided by the University of Panama, Veraguas Regional University Center, 2025
text_snippet: Level of Satisfaction of Undergraduate Students With the Academic and Administrative Services Provided by the University of Panama, Veraguas Regional University Center, 2025 The aim of the research is to analyze the level of satisfaction of students at the University of Panama, Veraguas Regional University Center, with the academic and administrative services it provides. The research has a non-experimental design based on a quantitative approach. The study is exploratory and descriptive; a questionnaire was developed based on the approaches of Do Santo, (2014) and Álvarez et al., (2015). It was found that 89.89% of the students surveyed were dissatisfied with academic services and 34.20% were dissatisfied with administrative services. They suggested updating the methodology applied, the teacher evaluation process, and improving customer service.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Recalibrating the Modern University Presidency: Structural Transformation, Leadership Preparation, and the Case for Enterprise Level Competence
text_snippet: Recalibrating the Modern University Presidency: Structural Transformation, Leadership Preparation, and the Case for Enterprise Level Competence The contemporary university presidency is undergoing structural transformation. Declining public confidence, shorter tenures, reduced state funding, heightened accountability, growing fundraising pressures, governance strain, commercialization demands, and political polarization are reshaping executive leadership. This study uses a structured integrative literature review with staged thematic synthesis to examine how these pressures alter the institutional environment and whether leadership preparation has adapted. Evidence draws on peer-reviewed scholarship and high-credibility sector data on trends in public trust, tenure, state finance, and philanthropy. Findings show a shift from internal stewardship to cross-domain leadership under volatile conditions. Six core domains emerge: strategic systems leadership, financial and resource orchestration, relational legitimacy, political intelligence and narrative leadership, entrepreneurial ecosystem integration, and adaptive resilience with ethical stewardship. Case illustrations indicate these domains are operational requirements, not aspirational traits. The study concludes that recalibrating presidential qualifications and preparatio

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Experiential Learning for Sustainability in Accounting: Leveraging ERPsim and Case Study Pedagogy
text_snippet: Experiential Learning for Sustainability in Accounting: Leveraging ERPsim and Case Study Pedagogy As sustainability reporting standards evolve, accounting and finance students must be prepared to apply ESG concepts in enterprise systems and decision‑making. This study introduces an experiential design integrating the ERPsim Logistics Sustainability Game with an adapted EYARC “Solar Energy” case in a Managerial Accounting course to strengthen understanding of sustainability in logistics, supply chains, and financial reporting. Grounded in experiential learning theory, the design enables students to use managerial accounting tools while making real‑time decisions in a live SAP ERP environment. Post‑simulation survey results show improved ESG comprehension, higher engagement, and strong support for integrating sustainability into ERP‑focused curricula.

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: AI in Healthcare Curricula: Preparing Future Healthcare Professionals for AI in the Workplace
text_snippet: AI in Healthcare Curricula: Preparing Future Healthcare Professionals for AI in the Workplace Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping healthcare delivery, offering new capabilities in diagnostics, treatment planning, patient management, and administrative efficiency. As these technologies rapidly expand across clinical and operational domains, healthcare professionals must be prepared to navigate both opportunities and challenges. This paper examines the need for integrating AI education into healthcare curricula to ensure graduates are equipped with the knowledge, skills, and ethical awareness required in an AI-driven workplace. Drawing on current research and emerging best practices, the implications of AI adoption for professional roles and competencies are highlighted, as are the barriers to effective curriculum design and strategies for embedding AI literacy within medical and health sciences education. Higher education institutions play a critical role in shaping the healthcare workforce’s readiness by fostering both technical fluency and critical reflection on AI’s societal impact. The manuscript concludes with recommendations for aligning curricula to support future healthcare professionals as competent, adaptive, and responsible users of AI technolog

journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: The Shadow Culture of Higher Education: Exploring Educational Pathways for Undocumented and DACA Students
text_snippet: The Shadow Culture of Higher Education: Exploring Educational Pathways for Undocumented and DACA Students This qualitative case study employed validation and organizational theories to explore the nuanced ways in which a private university validates, supports, and promotes the success of undocumented and DACAmented students. The findings revealed that an institutional “shadow culture” exists to mobilize access to resources, community, and foster success to degree completion. The authors theorize that students are validated and affirmed by resources and support services faculty and staff establish and sustain within the shadows of the institution.

title: Beyond the Brand: Utilizing the “Dud Index” for Academic Impact
text_snippet: Beyond the Brand: Utilizing the “Dud Index” for Academic Impact Google Gemini is a modern large language model (LLM) that has quickly become a “super tool for superusers.” Similar to garbage in, garbage out (GIGO) in statistics, in the hands of an expert user, Gemini is a tool indissoluble with speed and accuracy of answering important research questions. Knowing how to frame expert questions to prompt the LLM is essential. I ended up asking Gemini nine carefully crafted questions that evolved as Gemini answered each of my previous questions, respectively. By the time question #9 was answered, a “Dud Index” had been firmly established and justified. With the use of Gemini, I was able to developed a utility threshold to identify where journal “prestige” masks a lack of “utility.” This helps identify Type 1 Errors (False Positives: High rank but low impact) and Type 2 Errors (False Negatives: Low rank but high impact. journal_name: Journal of Higher Education Theory & Practice
title: Exploring Doctoral Students’ Thoughts about the Use of Artificial Intelligence for Learning
text_snippet: Exploring Doctoral Students’ Thoughts about the Use of Artificial Intelligence for Learning The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the classroom is a timely concept that needs more exploration to understand its impact. Therefore, we investigated this concept with four doctoral students in the United States and their written reflections about such topics. Participants were involved in a graduate-based mentoring program, where the directors of the program introduced the concept of AI-based tools as part of their monthly reflection work. Coding was conducted on the reflections with four themes prevailing: Ethical Concerns, Quality Work, Time-consuming, and Time-saver. Sample participant reflections, as well as implications for future research, were also detailed.

title: WhatsApp as a Vector of Language Change: Indications from Igbo Aboriginal Students in South-Western Nigerian Universities
text_snippet: WhatsApp as a Vector of Language Change: Indications from Igbo Aboriginal Students in South-Western Nigerian Universities Social media, especially WhatsApp, are increasingly shaping language use among young Nigerians at the expense of indigenous languages. This study examines the effect of WhatsApp on the use of the Igbo language among Igbo university students in southwestern Nigeria and how it may contribute to the endangerment of the Igbo language. The study draws on Media Ecology Theory, Technological Determinism Theory, and a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative surveys and interviews to examine how students engage with language on WhatsApp and whether the platform nurtures or undermines linguistic sustainability. Findings show that WhatsApp holds vast potential for the development of the Igbo language, which is currently neglected. The use of the Igbo language is principally confined to cultural or domestic contexts, while English language and Nigerian Pidgin are used in everyday media discussions. The absence of user consciousness that WhatsApp offers language-specific features contributes to the decline. title: Rethinking Assessment Practices for Multilingual Learners: Bridging Theory and Classroom Evidence in Mathematics Education
text_snippet: Rethinking Assessment Practices for Multilingual Learners: Bridging Theory and Classroom Evidence in Mathematics Education Mathematics assessments in higher education are often treated as neutral measures of student understanding, yet assessment design strongly shapes what multilingual learners (MLs) can demonstrate. Linguistic complexity, implicit curricular and cultural assumptions, and representational demands embedded in assessment tasks can obscure mathematical reasoning and compromise validity. This mixed empirical and conceptual study examines how common mathematics assessment practices function as barriers for MLs—not because of mathematical rigor, but because of avoidable design features. Analysis of assessment tasks, practitioner observations, and professional learning artifacts identifies three recurring barriers: linguistic density and ambiguity, hidden curricular and cultural assumptions, and representational overload. Situated within scholarship on language, validity, and equity in mathematics education, the findings illustrate how construct-irrelevant variance is introduced through assessment design in postsecondary and teacher preparation contexts. title: Visualizing Beyond the Mask: Black Collegians Cultivating Safety Through Joy
text_snippet: Visualizing Beyond the Mask: Black Collegians Cultivating Safety Through Joy This nationwide study examined how 25 Black undergraduate and graduate students defined and constructed the meaning of safety and joy on their campuses. Through our newly developed Critical Socioecological Framework for Racialized School Safety (CSFRSS), we address students’ experiences of cultivating joy within a liberatory framework, given that these students have historically been underserved and invalidated in academic spaces deemed unsafe. Using the study’ s data, we found that 1) feeling authentic–particularly within Black racial identity–was rooted in how students determined feeling safe, and 2) even in their unsafe academic spaces, students could cultivate joy due to their Black communities.
